required_features: Define core domain types and separate trusted domain objects from untrusted input.
Implement the main user workflow with explicit state and error behavior.
Validate external data and reject malformed or unauthorized inputs where applicable.
Add unit tests for ordinary values, edge cases, and at least one failure path.
Document compiler/runtime assumptions, setup commands, environment variables, and limitations.
stretch_features: Add one alternative design and explain the trade-off.
Add a regression test for a previously identified failure case.
Add CI checks for typechecking, linting, tests and reproducible builds.
test_plan: Run the configured type checker with the documented TypeScript version.
Run unit tests including invalid input, empty state and failure-path tests.
Run integration tests for each external boundary or mock it explicitly.
Review secrets, dependencies, permissions, logging and deployment settings.
Document what was tested and what has not been deployed or independently reviewed.

rubric.criterion: Type contracts and domain model correctness

review_method: Human-reviewed practical project with static artifact checks and learner-provided evidence. No arbitrary TypeScript code is executed by CodeLeaf; live service deployment is not performed by this course package.
status_note: Original project brief aligned with Section D of the supplied curriculum. Technical choices are illustrative; review runtime, library, security and deployment details before publication.
